# SQL CASE With ELSE Clause

#### Course: Learn SQL Basics

## SQL CASE With ELSE Clause

In the last example, the purchase_group column was empty for customers with a purchase_amount of 6000 or more because none of the WHEN conditions were met.

To address this, you can include an ELSE clause in the CASE statement to assign a default value when no conditions are met. For example,

```sql
1-- Default value of the purchase_group column is 'Premium Customer'
2-- if none of the conditions in the WHEN clauses are TRUE
3
4SELECT *,
5    CASE 
6        WHEN purchase_amount < 2000 THEN 'Low Spender'
7        WHEN purchase_amount >= 2000 AND purchase_amount < 5000 THEN 'Target Customer'
8        WHEN purchase_amount >= 5000 AND purchase_amount < 6000 THEN 'High Spender'
9        ELSE 'Premium Customer'
10    END AS purchase_group
11FROM Customers;
```
